answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The grove multiplier is published, charged in bridge, and delta lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1320 identities would post 4909 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
